messages:
maria-cs: Crescent reporting intermittent 401s and short 429 bursts during SDK startup in staging after an edge/WAF change. Ticket C-421.
liam-eng: Is it a single host? Can you paste a sanitized request example?
maria-cs: Single host. Example:
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}
They see ~1/10 401s and bursty 429s (~30s).
zara-ps: Likely causes: proxy/WAF trimming Authorization header, or very short token TTL causing refresh stampede. TTL?
maria-cs: Tokens TTL=15s, serverless pool with many pre-warmed workers.
sam-sre: Short TTL + synchronized refresh -> concurrent token requests -> 429s. Also proxies can drop Authorization -> 401. Ask them to add X-Debug-Id and run a probe to capture headers.
liam-eng: Probe: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Debug-Id:probe" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"probe"}'
Check whether Authorization arrives. If nginx in chain, ensure `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;`.
maria-cs: Customer logs (tokens redacted):
[09:20:13Z] 200 OK X-Debug-Id=probe req=1
[09:20:13Z] 401 Unauthorized X-Debug-Id=probe2 req=2 auth=missing
[09:20:14Z] 429 Too Many Requests X-Debug-Id=probe3 req=3 rate=client_concurrency
[09:20:15Z] 200 OK X-Debug-Id=probe4 req=4
They note auth sometimes missing.
sam-sre: Sounds like WAF/proxy stripping headers. Can they temporarily bypass the WAF?
maria-cs: They disabled suspect WAF groups and retried: result 10/10 200s; 429s largely gone after reducing refresh concurrency.
liam-eng: Next steps: 1) fix WAF rule to forward Authorization unchanged, 2) raise token TTL to ~60s and add jitter to refresh during rollout, 3) monitor and optionally provide a short elevated rate window for onboarding.
zara-ps: I'll draft a short onboarding checklist with nginx/envoy snippets and token guidance.
maria-cs: Updating ticket and requesting WAF post-mortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:
